Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns preparation of the NAIC Annual Statement Blank on a SAP basis for every writing company; reports to the Controller and escalates valuation judgements to the Chief Financial Officer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions and Blank (P&C/Life/Health as applicable), the NAIC Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual (SSAPs) as of the reporting year, and Arizona's financial reporting statute administered by the Arizona Department of Insurance and Financial Institutions (DIFI); re-read each October when the NAIC publishes the year's Blank and Instructions changes

In-scope processes.value: Year-end statutory close for the December 31 reporting year: GL lock, SAP adjustment posting, non-admitted asset determination, and build of Jurat, Pages 2-5, the Underwriting & Investment Exhibit, all investment and reinsurance schedules, Schedule P, Schedule T, Notes and General Interrogatories — plus the same build at Q1/Q2/Q3 for the quarterly Blank

In-scope systems.value: Annual statement preparation software holding the NAIC Blank, fed by the ERP general ledger trial balance, the investment accounting system, the reserving platform and the ceded reinsurance system

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statutory Annual Statement Preparation Procedure — close calendar, GL-to-Blank crosswalk by annual statement line, non-admitted asset test, schedule ownership matrix, cross-check clearance rules and Jurat sign-off protocol

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and refreshed every December against the NAIC Blank and Instructions changes issued by the Blanks (E) Working Group for the reporting year

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Statement must be complete, cross-check clean and officer-signed by February 20 so Regulatory Reporting can file by the March 1 statutory deadline; quarterly Blanks complete by May 8, August 8 and November 8 ahead of the 15th

Deadline reminders configured.value: Close calendar milestones fire at January 15 (GL lock), February 1 (all schedules drafted), February 10 (cross-checks clear), February 15 (actuarial opinion received) and February 20 (Jurat signed) to the Controller and Statutory Reporting Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Locked trial balance, GL-to-Blank crosswalk, schedule workpapers, cross-check clearance report and the signed Jurat page retained a minimum of 7 years from the statement date, and through the close of the next DIFI financial examination cycle

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any unexplained GL-to-Blank difference, unresolved cross-check edit, or post-filing restatement is logged with the affected annual statement page/line, the dollar effect, the root cause and the corrected-statement date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CFO signs off on every SAP adjustment above the reporting threshold, on every remaining cross-check override, and on any amended annual statement re-filed after March 1

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every annual statement page, exhibit and schedule prepared for each writing company for the reporting year, plus the underlying SAP adjustment journal entries booked between the GL close and the February 20 lock

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero unresolved NAIC cross-check or edit-check errors at filing; Page 2 total admitted assets and Page 3 surplus must tie to the locked trial balance to the dollar; any SAP adjustment without a SSAP reference or preparer/reviewer initials is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual with quarterly interim Blanks; the full test runs annually over the March 1 statement with a reduced tie-out test each quarter on Pages 2, 3 and 4

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared or reviewed any sampled schedule, and must sit outside the Controller organization

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual statement preparation test workpaper (trial balance tie-out, schedule sample, re-performance notes, cross-check re-run, exception log) filed in the compliance evidence repository under the reporting year and NAIC company code

Regulator-ready documentation.value: GL-to-Blank crosswalk, schedule workpapers and cross-check clearance report packaged as a DIFI financial examination request response, producible within 10 business days of an examiner information request

Regulator response path.value: The Statutory Reporting Manager answers DIFI and NAIC Financial Data Repository data-quality queries; the Chief Financial Officer clears any response that concedes a misstatement, and material corrections are re-filed as an amended statement

checklist.step: Lock the statutory close ledger and pull the year-end trial balance
actions: Confirm with the Finance Operations Analyst that all December subledger feeds (premium, claims, ceded, investment, payroll accrual) have posted and the period is at status 'Closed - no further postings'.
Run the trial balance for the reporting company at December 31 by legal entity and NAIC company code, exporting account number, account name, debit, credit and the statutory line mapping attribute.
Reconcile the trial balance control totals to the close/consolidation tool balance sheet and clear any difference before releasing it.
Publish the locked trial balance file as TB-<NAIC co-code>-<yyyy>-FINAL to the statutory close folder and notify the Statutory Reporting Manager that the Blank build can start.
checklist.done: a single locked, entity-level December 31 trial balance is published and no further postings are permitted to the reporting year.

checklist.step: Post the SAP adjustments that convert GAAP balances to statutory basis
actions: Work the standing SAP adjustment list with the Controller: deferred acquisition cost write-off, goodwill and intangible limits, deferred tax admissibility under SSAP No. 101, and prepaid/furniture non-admittance.
Book each adjustment in the statutory ledger with the SSAP reference in the journal description and the supporting schedule attached.
Compute the SSAP No. 101 paragraph 11 admitted deferred tax asset test (reversal window and surplus limit) and attach the calculation to the DTA entry.
Have a second preparer initial each adjustment above the reporting threshold and route the summary to the Chief Financial Officer.
File the adjustment register as the bridge between the GAAP and statutory trial balances.
checklist.done: every GAAP-to-SAP adjustment is booked with a SSAP citation, a support schedule and preparer plus reviewer initials.

checklist.step: Load the trial balance into the annual statement software against the Blank crosswalk
actions: Open the annual statement software, create the reporting year company file and set the Blank type (Property/Casualty, Life/Fraternal, or Health) to match the certificate of authority.
Import the locked trial balance and run the mapping report showing each GL account against its annual statement page and line.
Investigate every unmapped account with the Senior Accountant who owns it and assign a page/line before proceeding - never let an account default to 'Aggregate write-ins'.
Confirm the imported total assets and total surplus agree to the trial balance to the dollar and record the tie-out in the workpaper.
Update the crosswalk document for any new account added during the year.
checklist.done: every GL account is mapped to a named annual statement page and line and the imported totals tie exactly to the locked trial balance.

checklist.step: Build Page 2 Assets and prove the non-admitted asset column
actions: Populate Page 2 columns 1 (Assets), 2 (Non-admitted Assets) and 3 (Net Admitted Assets) for every asset line.

Apply the non-admittance rules line by line: agents' balances over 90 days past due, EDP equipment above the SSAP No. 16 limit, furniture and supplies, and the SSAP No. 101 non-admitted deferred tax asset.
Pull the premium receivable aging from the billing system and prove the over-90-day balance that drives the non-admitted uncollected premium figure.
Confirm Page 2 line 28 net admitted assets equals Page 3 line 28 total liabilities plus surplus.
Save the non-admitted asset workpaper with the aging extract attached.
checklist.done: Page 2 foots, ties to Page 3, and each non-admitted amount is supported by a named SSAP rule and a source extract.

checklist.step: Build Page 3 Liabilities, Surplus and Other Funds with the reserve owners
actions: Take the booked loss and loss adjustment expense reserves, gross and net of reinsurance, from the Reserving Actuary's year-end reserve report and load them to Page 3 lines 1 and 3.
Take unearned premium from the policy administration system's UPR register and reconcile it to the GL unearned premium account before loading line 9.
Load the provision for reinsurance computed on Schedule F Part 3 and confirm the change flows to the surplus account on Page 4.

Reconcile capital and surplus roll-forward: prior year-end surplus plus net income plus change in unrealized plus change in non-admitted plus change in provision for reinsurance equals current surplus.
Send the surplus roll-forward to the Chief Financial Officer with each reconciling item named.
checklist.done: Page 3 is complete, loss reserves agree to the actuarial reserve report, and the surplus roll-forward explains every dollar of movement.

checklist.step: Build the Statement of Income and the Underwriting & Investment Exhibit
actions: Populate the Underwriting & Investment Exhibit Part 1 (premiums earned), Part 1A (recapitulation of all premiums), Part 1B (premiums written by line), Part 2 (losses paid and incurred) and Part 3 (expenses).
Allocate other underwriting expenses across loss adjustment, acquisition and general expense using the SSAP No. 70 allocation basis and attach the allocation schedule.
Carry Part 1 earned premium, Part 2 incurred losses and Part 3 expenses to Page 4 lines 1, 2 and 4 and confirm the software carry-forwards match your manual figures.
Reconcile net investment income earned on Page 4 to the Exhibit of Net Investment Income and to the investment accounting income report.
Tie net income on Page 4 to the surplus roll-forward on Page 4 line 22.
checklist.done: the Underwriting & Investment Exhibit foots to Page 4 and net investment income agrees to the investment accounting system.

checklist.step: Build the investment schedules from the investment accounting system
actions: Export the December 31 holdings file with CUSIP, description, acquisition date, book/adjusted carrying value, fair value, par, NAIC designation and SVO administrative symbol.

Build Schedule D Part 1 (bonds) and Part 2 (stocks) and the acquisition/disposition Parts 3, 4 and 5, applying amortized cost for bonds designated NAIC 1-5 and lower of cost or fair value where required.

Build Schedule DA (short-term investments), Schedule DB Parts A-D (derivatives with counterparty and notional), Schedule DL (securities lending collateral) and Schedule E Parts 1-3 (cash, cash equivalents and special deposits).
Confirm every NAIC designation against the NAIC Securities Valuation Office filing exempt or SVO-assigned designation, and list any security without a designation for the Chief Investment Officer.
Tie Schedule D Part 1 and Part 2 totals plus Schedules DA and E to the Page 2 invested asset lines to the dollar.
Attach the custodian statement as the third-party support for the holdings file.
checklist.done: every investment schedule agrees to the custodian statement and to the Page 2 invested asset lines, with an NAIC designation on every security.

checklist.step: Build Schedule F and compute the provision for reinsurance
actions: Extract ceded balances by reinsurer: paid loss recoverable, unpaid loss and LAE recoverable, unearned premium ceded, funds held and collateral held.
Populate Schedule F Part 1 (assumed) and Part 2 (ceded) keyed by each reinsurer's NAIC company code and FEIN, flagging authorized, unauthorized and certified status per the domiciliary state's list.
Age the ceded paid loss recoverables over 90 days past due and enter the slow-paying reinsurer amounts that drive the Part 3 penalty.
Compute the provision for reinsurance on Schedule F Part 3 using unauthorized balances net of qualifying collateral plus the overdue authorized penalty, and carry the total to Page 3.
Reconcile total ceded recoverable on Schedule F to the ceded balance in the general ledger and explain any difference in the workpaper.
checklist.done: Schedule F is complete by reinsurer with authorization status, the provision for reinsurance is computed and carried to Page 3, and ceded totals tie to the GL.

checklist.step: Build Schedule P loss development with the Reserving Actuary
actions: Extract paid losses, case reserves and defense and cost containment expense by accident year and line of business from the claims data warehouse for the ten most recent accident years.

Populate Schedule P Part 1 (cumulative paid and incurred by accident year), Part 2 (incurred net loss development), Part 3 (cumulative paid net loss development) and Part 4 (bulk and IBNR reserves) for each Part 1 line.
Confirm the Part 1 Column for total net losses and expenses unpaid ties to the Page 3 loss and LAE reserve lines.
Complete Schedule P Interrogatories, including the question on whether the company has excess statutory reserves and the discounting disclosures.
Hand the completed triangles to the Appointed Actuary as the data behind the Statement of Actuarial Opinion.
checklist.done: Schedule P is populated for all Part 1 lines and ten accident years, and the unpaid total agrees to Page 3.

checklist.step: Build Schedule T and the state allocation of premium
actions: Extract direct premiums written and direct losses paid by state of risk for all 51 jurisdictions plus Canada and other alien exposure.
Populate Schedule T - Exhibit of Premiums Written, entering the state, the direct premiums written, direct premiums earned, direct losses paid and direct losses unpaid on each state row.
Confirm the Schedule T grand total direct premium written equals the Underwriting & Investment Exhibit Part 1B direct written total.
Flag any state showing premium where the company holds no certificate of authority and hand the list to the Compliance Officer for licensing review before filing.
Reconcile the Schedule T state figures to the premium tax return worksheets prepared by the Tax Manager.
checklist.done: Schedule T covers every jurisdiction with premium, ties to Part 1B, and no unlicensed-state premium is left unexplained.

checklist.step: Complete the Notes to Financial Statements and General Interrogatories
actions: Work the Notes to Financial Statements in Blank order, completing every note including permitted practices, going concern, related party transactions, reinsurance, and the SSAP No. 101 income tax note tables.
Answer General Interrogatories Part 1 (general) and Part 2 (property/casualty or life specific) question by question, and attach the required list where a 'Yes' answer demands one.
Collect the holding company organizational chart from the Corporate Secretary and complete Schedule Y Part 1 and Part 1A, with FEIN and NAIC code on each affiliate.
Complete the Five-Year Historical Data page and confirm the prior-year columns agree to the statements as previously filed.
Route the notes and interrogatories to the General Counsel for the litigation and related-party answers.
checklist.done: no note or interrogatory is left blank or answered 'N/A' without support, and Schedule Y matches the current holding company chart.

checklist.step: Run the NAIC cross-check and edit-check validations and clear every error
actions: In the annual statement software run the full validation set: cross-checks (page-to-schedule ties), edit checks (Blank-level rules) and the prior-year comparison edits.
Work the error report top to bottom, correcting the source data rather than the Blank cell wherever the error points to a feed.
For any edit that must be answered rather than corrected, write the explanation the NAIC Financial Data Repository will accept and record who approved it.
Re-run validations until the error count is zero and print the clean validation report to the workpaper.
Notify the Controller and the Regulatory Reporting Manager that the statement is validation-clean and ready for opinion and signature.
checklist.done: the validation report shows zero unresolved cross-check and edit-check errors and is filed in the workpaper.

checklist.step: Run the Risk-Based Capital calculation and reconcile it to the statement
actions: Load the completed annual statement into the NAIC RBC formula and populate the asset risk, credit risk, underwriting risk and off-balance-sheet pages.
Confirm the RBC input pages pull the same Schedule D designations, Schedule F recoverables and Schedule P reserves that the statement reports - any difference means one of the two is wrong.
Compute total adjusted capital and the authorized control level, and state the RBC ratio for the Chief Financial Officer.
Where the ratio falls into any RBC action level, notify the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Risk Officer the same day so the required plan is started.
File the RBC report for filing with the annual statement by the same March 1 deadline.
checklist.done: RBC is computed from the filed statement figures, the ratio is reported to the CFO, and any action level is escalated the day it is known.

checklist.step: Obtain the Statement of Actuarial Opinion and tie it to the reported reserves
actions: Confirm the Appointed Actuary's appointment is board-approved and on record with the domiciliary regulator before opining.

Perform the reserve analysis on the Schedule P data and issue the Statement of Actuarial Opinion in the NAIC-prescribed form, stating the opinion type (unqualified, qualified, adverse or inconclusive).
Confirm the reserve amounts identified in the SCOPE paragraph agree exactly to Page 3 loss and LAE reserve lines and to Schedule P Part 1.
Prepare the confidential Actuarial Opinion Summary with the actuary's point estimate and range for filing with the domiciliary regulator by March 15.
Deliver the signed opinion and the Actuarial Report backing it to the Statutory Reporting Manager by February 15.
checklist.done: a signed Statement of Actuarial Opinion is on hand by February 15 with SCOPE amounts tying to Page 3 and Schedule P.

checklist.step: Obtain officer signatures on the Jurat page and lock the statement
actions: Review the Jurat page for accuracy: company name, NAIC company code, NAIC group code, FEIN, state of domicile, statutory home office address and the list of officers and directors.

Have the president, secretary and the chief financial officer sign the Jurat attesting the statement is a full and true statement of all assets, liabilities, income and deductions on the NAIC-prescribed basis.
Obtain notarization where the domiciliary state requires a sworn Jurat and record which states demand a notarized original.
Lock the statement file in the annual statement software so no cell can change after signature, and record the lock date and time.
Hand the locked, signed statement to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for filing, with the actuarial opinion and RBC report attached.
checklist.done: the Jurat carries all required officer signatures and the correct NAIC codes, the file is locked, and the package is handed to Regulatory Reporting before February 20.

testing.step: Build the population of statement components subject to test
actions: List every page, exhibit, schedule and supplement in the filed annual statement for each writing company and NAIC company code for the reporting year.
Add the SAP adjustment journal register covering entries booked between the GL close and the February 20 lock.
Reconcile the component list to the NAIC Blank table of contents for the company's Blank type so no required schedule is missing from the population.
Sign the population as complete and record the extraction date and the statement version identifier.
testing.done: the population covers every required Blank component plus the SAP adjustment register and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the filed statement back to the locked general ledger
actions: Pull the locked December 31 trial balance independently from the ERP rather than accepting the preparer's copy.
Foot Page 2 net admitted assets and Page 3 total liabilities plus surplus and compare both to the trial balance plus the SAP adjustment register.
Trace each reconciling item to a specific adjustment journal with a SSAP reference; an unexplained difference of any size is an exception.
Confirm the prior-year columns on Pages 2, 3 and 4 agree to the statement as previously filed with the NAIC.
testing.done: Page 2 and Page 3 tie to the ledger to the dollar and every reconciling item traces to a cited SAP adjustment.

testing.step: Draw and document the schedule sample
actions: Take 100% of Schedule D Part 1, Schedule F Part 3, Schedule P Part 1 and Schedule T - these carry the highest regulator scrutiny.
Select 40 line-item detail rows at random (seeded, reproducible) across Schedules A, B, BA, DA, DB, DL and E.
Select 15 SAP adjustment journals stratified so every entry above the reporting threshold is included.
Record the seed, the population counts and the selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn by an examiner.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers the four high-risk schedules in full, and the selection method is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the non-admitted asset determination
actions: Pull the premium receivable aging directly from the billing system at December 31 and recompute the balance over 90 days past due.
Recompute the SSAP No. 101 admitted deferred tax asset using the reversal period and the surplus limitation and compare to the amount reported.
Check that EDP equipment, furniture, supplies and prepaid expenses are non-admitted in full on Page 2 column 2.
Report any difference between your recomputation and the filed Page 2 column 2 as an exception with the dollar effect on surplus.
testing.done: each non-admitted category is independently recomputed and any variance is quantified against reported surplus.

testing.step: Re-perform Schedule D valuation and NAIC designations
actions: Obtain the December 31 custodian statement independently and compare CUSIP-level par and holdings to Schedule D Parts 1 and 2.
For 25 sampled bonds, recompute amortized cost from acquisition date, cost and par, and compare to the reported book/adjusted carrying value.
Verify each sampled security's NAIC designation against the SVO assignment or filing exempt rating, and confirm any 6-designated security is carried at the lower of amortized cost or fair value.
Confirm Schedule D totals plus Schedules DA and E agree to the Page 2 invested asset lines.
testing.done: sampled securities tie to the custodian statement, carrying values recompute, and every designation is independently verified.

testing.step: Re-perform the Schedule F provision for reinsurance
actions: For each reinsurer on Schedule F Part 2, independently confirm authorized, unauthorized or certified status against the domiciliary state's list of accredited and certified reinsurers as of December 31.

Recompute the unauthorized reinsurance provision as unauthorized balances less qualifying letters of credit, trust and funds-held collateral, checking each letter of credit is clean, irrevocable and evergreen.
Recompute the overdue authorized reinsurance penalty using the over-90-day paid recoverable aging.
Compare your total to the provision for reinsurance reported on Page 3 and quantify any difference as a surplus misstatement.
testing.done: the provision for reinsurance is independently recomputed and every reinsurer's authorization status is verified against the regulator's list.

testing.step: Trace Schedule P and Schedule T to their source systems
actions: Extract paid loss and case reserve totals by accident year and Schedule P line directly from the claims system and compare to Schedule P Part 1.
Confirm Schedule P Part 1 total net losses and expenses unpaid agrees to Page 3 lines 1 and 3.
Extract direct written premium by state of risk from the policy administration system and compare state by state to Schedule T.
Compare the Schedule T grand total to the Underwriting & Investment Exhibit Part 1B direct written total and to the premium tax return worksheets.
testing.done: Schedule P and Schedule T both trace to independent system extracts and tie to the statement pages that depend on them.

testing.step: Re-run the NAIC validations and recompute the RBC ratio
actions: Open the locked, filed statement file and re-run the full cross-check and edit-check validation set yourself.
Confirm the error count is zero; where an edit was answered with an explanation rather than corrected, read the explanation and judge whether the underlying number is right.
Recompute total adjusted capital and the authorized control level from the filed statement and compare the resulting RBC ratio to the filed RBC report.
Confirm the Jurat page carries the correct NAIC company code, group code and FEIN and bears all required officer signatures with the notarization the domiciliary state demands.
testing.done: validations re-run clean on the filed file, the RBC ratio recomputes, and the Jurat is complete and correctly coded.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception recording the annual statement page/line, the dollar effect, the effect on surplus and the affected NAIC company code.
Assign a root cause (source feed error, mapping gap, missed SSAP application, manual override, late actuarial input) and a named owner in Finance or Actuarial.
Set a remediation date ahead of the next quarterly Blank, and for any misstatement that changes reported surplus, open an amended-statement assessment with the Chief Financial Officer.
Carry every open exception into the next reporting year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries a page/line reference, a surplus effect, a root cause, an owner and a remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and the aggregate surplus effect and compare both to the zero-unresolved-error threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared no sampled schedule and sits outside the Controller organization, sign the workpaper.
Report the results and any surplus-affecting misstatement to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper under the reporting year and NAIC company code.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with a stated conclusion, the aggregate surplus effect and an Audit Committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns transmission of the annual and quarterly statements to the NAIC Financial Data Repository and to all 51 jurisdictions, and owns the proof-of-timely-filing file

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alaska's financial reporting statute administered by the Alaska Division of Insurance for the domiciliary-style filing, plus the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions state filing checklist appendix that lists, jurisdiction by jurisdiction, what must be filed with the state versus with the NAIC and in what medium

In-scope processes.value: Post-signature filing execution: NAIC Financial Data Repository electronic submission, per-state hard-copy and PDF submissions, filing fee payment, barcode cover-sheet generation, and capture of every acknowledgement for the annual (March 1) and quarterly (May 15, August 15, November 15) statements

In-scope systems.value: Annual statement software export to the NAIC Financial Data Repository via iSite+, with acknowledgements and state confirmations filed in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statutory Filing Transmission Procedure — export and validate the NAIC data file, submit to the Financial Data Repository, work the state filing checklist jurisdiction by jurisdiction, pay fees, and capture the confirmation for each

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Controller and re-approved each January after the NAIC publishes the reporting year's state filing checklist and any state issues a bulletin changing its submission medium

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual statement and RBC report by March 1; Actuarial Opinion Summary by March 15; quarterly statements by May 15, August 15 and November 15; every jurisdiction's own due date and any state that demands receipt rather than postmark by the deadline

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar alerts at T-21, T-10, T-3 and T-1 business days before March 1 and before each quarterly 15th, addressed to the Regulatory Reporting Manager with escalation to the Controller at T-3 if any jurisdiction is still open

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: NAIC Financial Data Repository submission receipts, per-state acknowledgement emails and portal confirmations, courier tracking records for hard-copy states, and fee payment confirmations retained 7 years from the filing date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any jurisdiction filed after its due date, any rejected NAIC submission, and any missing confirmation is logged with the jurisdiction, the days late, the penalty assessed and the corrective action

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Controller signs off on every late or rejected filing, on the explanation letter sent to the affected regulator, and on the payment of any late-filing penalty

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every jurisdiction-filing pairing for the reporting year: 51 jurisdictions plus the NAIC, times each writing company, times the annual statement and the three quarterly statements

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any jurisdiction filing with no confirmation on file, or with a confirmation dated after that jurisdiction's due date, is a fail; a single late jurisdiction escalates to the Chief Financial Officer

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation recurs four times a year; test runs after each filing cycle over that cycle's jurisdiction population, with the March 1 cycle tested in full including fee payment and medium

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have transmitted any sampled filing and must not sit in the Regulatory Reporting team

Evidence location for test results.value: Filing timeliness test workpaper (jurisdiction matrix, confirmation captures, due-date recomputation, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository, indexed by filing cycle and NAIC company code

Regulator-ready documentation.value: A jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction filing register with the submission date, the confirmation identifier and the acknowledgement image, producible for a Division of Insurance timeliness inquiry within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Reporting Manager answers state filing-desk queries and NAIC Financial Data Repository rejection notices; the Controller clears any correspondence admitting a late filing, and General Counsel is engaged where a penalty or administrative action follows

checklist.step: Confirm the statement is signed, locked and cleared for transmission
actions: Receive the locked statement file from the Statutory Reporting Manager and confirm the file is at status Locked with the lock date recorded.
Check the Jurat page carries the president, secretary and chief financial officer signatures and, where the domiciliary state requires it, a notary seal.
Confirm the Statement of Actuarial Opinion, the RBC report and the required March 1 supplements are in the package before opening the transmission window.
Refuse transmission of any package missing a signature, the opinion or a required supplement and return it to the Controller with the missing items named.
checklist.done: the package is signed, locked, opinion-attached and formally accepted by Regulatory Reporting for transmission.

checklist.step: Refresh the state filing checklist for the reporting year
actions: Open the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions and go to the state filing checklist appendix that lists each jurisdiction's required filings.

For each of the 51 jurisdictions record: whether the annual statement is required with the state or NAIC-only, the required medium (electronic, PDF, printed original), the number of copies, whether a notarized Jurat is demanded, the filing fee and the due date.
Cross-read each state's insurance department bulletin page for any change to the medium or fee issued since the checklist was published.
Update the jurisdiction matrix in the internal regulatory system and mark each row with the date the state's requirement was last verified.
Send the changed rows to the Regulatory Reporting Manager so the transmission plan reflects them.
checklist.done: all 51 jurisdiction rows carry a medium, copy count, fee, due date and a verification date inside the current filing year.

checklist.step: Export and validate the NAIC electronic filing data file
actions: In the annual statement software run the NAIC electronic filing export to produce the data file and the accompanying PDF of the complete Blank.

Run the software's pre-submission validation against the NAIC file format specification and confirm the header carries the correct NAIC company code, group code, FEIN, Blank type and reporting period.
Compare the exported file's total admitted assets, total liabilities and surplus figures to the printed Page 2 and Page 3 to prove the export did not truncate.
Save the export and its validation log as the pre-submission evidence for the cycle.
checklist.done: an export file passes format validation, carries the correct company identifiers, and its key totals match the printed statement.

checklist.step: Submit the annual statement to the NAIC Financial Data Repository
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ with the company's filing credentials and open the Financial Data Repository annual statement upload function.
Select the reporting year, the company by NAIC code and the Blank type, then upload the export data file and the PDF Blank.
Wait for the repository's processing result and read the acceptance or rejection notice in full rather than assuming success.
Where the file is rejected, correct the underlying data with the Statutory Reporting Manager, re-lock, re-export and resubmit the same day - never let a rejection sit overnight near the deadline.
Download the submission confirmation showing the date, time and file identifier and file it as the primary proof of the March 1 filing.
checklist.done: the NAIC Financial Data Repository shows the statement accepted for the reporting year and the dated confirmation is saved.

checklist.step: Generate the barcode cover sheets required for supplemental and state filings
actions: For every document the NAIC requires as a separate barcoded filing (actuarial opinion, supplements, audited financials), generate the NAIC document filing barcode cover sheet from the annual statement software.
Check each cover sheet carries the correct NAIC company code, reporting year, document type code and the filer contact.
Attach the cover sheet as the first page of the PDF for each document so the repository routes it to the right document type.
Keep a register of the barcode identifiers generated so a later query can be answered without regenerating them.
checklist.done: each separately filed document carries a correct NAIC barcode cover sheet and its identifier is recorded in the register.

checklist.step: File with the domiciliary Division of Insurance
actions: Read the domiciliary state's row on the jurisdiction matrix - for the Alaska Division of Insurance file the signed annual statement, actuarial opinion and RBC report by March 1 in the medium the Division specifies.
Submit through the state's filing channel (department portal upload or the filing desk email address published on the Division's website), naming the file <company>-<NAIC code>-AS-<yyyy>.
Pay the state's annual statement filing fee through the state's payment channel and save the payment confirmation number.
Request and retain the Division's written acknowledgement; where none is issued automatically, email the filing desk asking for confirmation of receipt and file the reply.
Record the submission date, channel, fee paid and confirmation identifier on the domiciliary row of the filing register.
checklist.done: the domiciliary Division has the complete package on or before March 1 with a retained acknowledgement and fee confirmation.

checklist.step: Work the remaining jurisdictions row by row through the filing register
actions: Take the jurisdiction matrix in due-date order and open a filing register row for each of the 51 jurisdictions for the reporting year.
For NAIC-only states, record that the Financial Data Repository submission satisfies the requirement and reference the repository confirmation identifier.
For states requiring their own copy, submit through that state's portal or filing email and enter the submission date and confirmation on the register row.
For states still requiring a printed original, print the statement, obtain the notarized Jurat where demanded, and dispatch by trackable courier with signature on delivery.
Leave no register row blank - a row with no confirmation is treated as unfiled until proven otherwise.
checklist.done: every one of the 51 jurisdiction rows shows a submission date, a channel and a confirmation or courier tracking number.

checklist.step: Pay every jurisdiction's filing fee and match the payment to the filing
actions: Take the fee column from the jurisdiction matrix and raise the payment run for the states charging an annual statement filing fee.
Pay through each state's accepted method (department portal card or ACH, OPTins electronic payment, or check to the address on the state's fee schedule) and record the method used.
Match each payment confirmation number to its filing register row so fee and filing are provably paired.
Report any state rejecting a payment to the Regulatory Reporting Manager the same day, because an unpaid fee can render the filing incomplete.
checklist.done: every fee-charging jurisdiction has a matched payment confirmation on its filing register row.

checklist.step: Capture and index every acknowledgement as proof of timely filing
actions: Download or screenshot each state portal confirmation and save it as <state>-<NAIC code>-AS-<yyyy>-confirmation.pdf.
Save the acknowledgement email including full headers so the received timestamp survives, and the courier proof-of-delivery for hard-copy states.
Upload the whole set to the compliance evidence repository indexed by jurisdiction, reporting year, company code and filing type.
Chase any jurisdiction with no confirmation within 5 business days of submission by emailing the state's filing desk and logging the chase.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction has an indexed, dated proof of receipt in the evidence repository or an open, logged chase.

checklist.step: File the Actuarial Opinion Summary and the confidential filings on their own deadlines
actions: Take the confidential Actuarial Opinion Summary from the Appointed Actuary and file it with the domiciliary regulator by March 15 - it goes to the state, not to the NAIC public repository.
File the Actuarial Report and underlying workpapers with the domiciliary regulator on request within the period the state's request allows.
Mark each confidential filing as confidential in the transmission and record which jurisdictions received it.
Confirm receipt with the domiciliary regulator's actuarial unit and file the acknowledgement separately from the public filing evidence.
checklist.done: the Actuarial Opinion Summary is filed by March 15 with a retained confidential-filing acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly statement transmission on the same discipline
actions: For Q1, Q2 and Q3 export the quarterly Blank and upload it to the NAIC Financial Data Repository ahead of May 15, August 15 and November 15.
Work the jurisdiction matrix quarterly column, which differs from the annual column - several states take quarterly statements NAIC-only.
Capture the repository confirmation and any state confirmation onto the quarterly filing register rows.
Report the quarterly filing status to the Controller within 3 business days of each deadline.
checklist.done: each quarterly cycle closes with a complete register and a status report to the Controller within 3 business days of the 15th.

checklist.step: Reconcile the filing register to the jurisdiction matrix before declaring the cycle closed
actions: Count the jurisdiction matrix rows requiring a filing for the cycle and count the filing register rows carrying a confirmation.
Investigate every difference by name - a missing row is either a state that does not require the filing (with the checklist reference proving it) or an unfiled state.
Confirm each confirmation date is on or before that jurisdiction's own due date, using the state's rule on receipt versus postmark.
Declare the cycle closed in writing to the Controller only when the two counts agree and every date passes.
checklist.done: matrix and register counts agree, every confirmation pre-dates its due date, and the cycle closure is confirmed in writing.

checklist.step: Handle rejections, resubmissions and amended statements
actions: Monitor the NAIC Financial Data Repository and state filing desks for rejection or data-quality notices for 30 days after each submission.
For each notice, identify whether the fault is format (re-export and resubmit) or content (correct the statement, re-lock, obtain re-signature where the Jurat figures change).
Where a corrected statement changes reported surplus, prepare an amended annual statement, mark it amended, and re-file it to the NAIC and every jurisdiction that received the original.
Write to the domiciliary Division explaining the amendment, what changed and why, and log the exchange.
checklist.done: no rejection or data-quality notice is open beyond its response window and every amendment reaches all jurisdictions that received the original.

checklist.step: Escalate any jurisdiction that will miss its deadline
actions: At T-3 business days review the open jurisdiction list from the filing register with the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
For any jurisdiction that cannot be filed on time, contact that state's filing desk before the deadline to request an extension and record the request, the person contacted and the answer.
Notify the Chief Financial Officer the same day a deadline is confirmed missed, with the jurisdiction, the reason and the expected penalty.
Record the decision and its owner on the register row - filing an incomplete statement to beat the clock is never one of the options.
checklist.done: every at-risk jurisdiction has a pre-deadline regulator contact or a written, owned decision escalated to the CFO.

checklist.step: Archive the filing evidence set for the reporting year
actions: Assemble the filed statement PDF, the NAIC repository confirmation, all 51 jurisdiction confirmations, courier proofs and fee payment records into one reporting-year evidence set.
Apply the 7-year retention label running from the March 1 filing date, extended through the close of the next financial examination.
Confirm the repository index makes the set searchable by jurisdiction, NAIC company code, reporting year and filing type.
Hand the index reference to the Statutory Reporting Manager and the Chief Audit Executive.
checklist.done: the reporting-year filing evidence set is complete, retention-labelled and retrievable by jurisdiction and company code.

testing.step: Build the population of jurisdiction filings owed for the cycle
actions: Extract the jurisdiction matrix rows for the reporting year and expand them by writing company and by filing cycle (annual plus three quarterlies).
Independently confirm the row count against the number of jurisdictions in which the company holds a certificate of authority, taken from the licensing register.
Confirm each row's stated requirement against the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions state filing checklist rather than the internal matrix alone.
Sign the population as complete and note the extraction date.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the licensing register and to the NAIC state filing checklist, and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the filing register to the population
actions: Match each population row to a filing register row on jurisdiction plus company plus cycle.
List every population row with no register row and every register row with no confirmation as automatic exceptions.
Check that any row claiming 'NAIC-only, no state filing required' cites the state filing checklist page proving it.
Quantify the unmatched count before any sampling begins.
testing.done: every owed filing is matched to a confirmed register row or listed as an exception with the count stated.

testing.step: Draw and document the jurisdiction sample
actions: Take 100% of the domiciliary jurisdiction and of any jurisdiction requiring a printed original or a notarized Jurat.
Select 20 further jurisdictions at random (seeded, reproducible) across the annual and quarterly cycles.
Include 100% of jurisdictions with a prior-year late filing or penalty.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn by an examiner.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers the domiciliary and hard-copy states in full, and includes every prior-year late jurisdiction.

testing.step: Re-perform the NAIC repository submission check
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ independently and open the Financial Data Repository filing history for the company's NAIC code and reporting year.
Confirm an accepted annual statement submission exists, and read the acceptance date and file identifier straight from the repository rather than the internal register.
Confirm the separately barcoded documents (actuarial opinion, supplements, audited financials) appear against the right document types.
Note any submission the repository shows as rejected or superseded that the internal register records as accepted.
testing.done: repository filing history independently confirms acceptance and document types, and any register-to-repository difference is noted.

testing.step: Trace each sampled jurisdiction to its confirmation and identifier
actions: Open the stored confirmation for each sampled jurisdiction and read the confirmation identifier, the submitting entity and the date directly off the artifact.
For hard-copy states, read the courier proof-of-delivery signature and date rather than the dispatch date.
Confirm the confirmation names the correct company and NAIC company code - a confirmation for an affiliate does not prove this company filed.
Treat a screenshot with no visible date, identifier or company name as no evidence at all.
testing.done: each sampled jurisdiction has a dated, identified confirmation naming the correct company, or is logged as unevidenced.

testing.step: Recompute the timeliness of every sampled filing
actions: Read each sampled jurisdiction's own due date from the state filing checklist (annual March 1; quarterlies May 15, August 15, November 15 unless the state differs).
Apply the state's rule on whether the deadline is met by transmission, by postmark or by receipt.
Compute days late as confirmation date minus due date for every sampled row and list any positive result.
Confirm the Actuarial Opinion Summary was filed with the domiciliary regulator by March 15 and the RBC report by March 1.
testing.done: days-late is computed for every sampled jurisdiction on that state's own rule, and every positive value is listed.

testing.step: Verify fee payment and submission medium against the state's requirement
actions: For each sampled fee-charging jurisdiction, trace the payment to a cleared disbursement in the ledger and to the payment confirmation number on the register row.
Compare the amount paid to the state's published fee schedule for the reporting year.
Confirm the medium actually used (portal upload, email, printed original, notarized Jurat) matches what the state filing checklist requires.
Flag any filing accepted in a medium the state does not permit, because acceptance does not cure a defective filing.
testing.done: each sampled fee traces to a cleared payment at the published amount and every submission medium matches the state's requirement.

testing.step: Test rejection handling and amended-statement completeness
actions: Pull every rejection or data-quality notice received during the cycle from the tracker and from the repository history.
Confirm each was resolved and resubmitted, and compute the elapsed days between notice and successful resubmission.
For any amended annual statement, confirm it reached the NAIC and every jurisdiction that received the original, by matching the amendment distribution list to the original filing register.
Treat any amendment that reached fewer jurisdictions than the original as a reportable exception.
testing.done: every rejection has a dated resolution and every amendment provably reached the full original distribution.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the jurisdiction, cycle, days late or missing evidence, and any penalty assessed by the state.
Assign a root cause (stale jurisdiction matrix, missed medium change, repository rejection worked too late, fee unpaid, confirmation never chased) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date ahead of the next quarterly cycle and, for any late domiciliary filing, open a regulator-communication assessment with the Controller.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a jurisdiction, days-late figure, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate across all 51 jurisdictions and compare to the zero-late threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references and the list of late or unevidenced jurisdictions.
Have the independent reviewer, who transmitted none of the sampled filings and sits outside Regulatory Reporting, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper by filing cycle and NAIC company code.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with the on-time rate, a stated conclusion and an Audit Committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the inventory of NAIC supplements, exhibits and interrogatories due with and after the March 1 annual statement, and the assignment of each to a named preparer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions supplement index (which lists each supplement, its due date of March 1, March 15, April 1, June 1 or August 1, and whether it is filed with the state, the NAIC, or both), read alongside the Alaska Division of Insurance financial reporting statute for the domiciliary requirement

In-scope processes.value: Preparation of the supplemental filings that accompany the statutory annual statement: Supplemental Compensation Exhibit, Schedule SIS, Reinsurance Attestation Supplement, Trusteed Surplus Statement, Medicare Supplement Insurance Experience Exhibit, Management's Discussion and Analysis, Supplemental Investment Risk Interrogatories, Accident and Health Policy Experience Exhibit, Credit Insurance Experience Exhibit and Long-Term Care Experience Reporting Forms

In-scope systems.value: Supplement templates within the annual statement software, fed by the HR compensation system, the ceded reinsurance system, the investment accounting system and the policy administration experience extracts

Compliance procedure documented.value: Annual Statement Supplement Procedure — supplement applicability test by Blank type and line of business, preparer/reviewer assignment matrix, source-data owner per supplement, and the not-applicable justification standard

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Controller and refreshed every November when the NAIC Blanks (E) Working Group adopts the reporting year's supplement changes

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: March 1 supplements (Supplemental Compensation Exhibit, Schedule SIS, Reinsurance Attestation Supplement, Trusteed Surplus Statement, Medicare Supplement Insurance Experience Exhibit); March 15 Actuarial Opinion Summary; April 1 supplements (Management's Discussion and Analysis, Supplemental Investment Risk Interrogatories, Accident and Health Policy Experience Exhibit, Credit Insurance Experience Exhibit, Long-Term Care Experience Reporting Forms)

Deadline reminders configured.value: Two reminder tracks - the March 1 supplement track alerting at January 20, February 10 and February 24, and the April 1 track alerting at March 5, March 20 and March 27, each addressed to the named supplement preparer and copied to the Statutory Reporting Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Each supplement's source extract, preparation workpaper, reviewer sign-off and the barcoded filed PDF retained 7 years from the March 1 statement date, together with the not-applicable justification for every supplement not filed

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any supplement filed after its March 1 or April 1 date, filed with a source-data difference, or omitted without a documented not-applicable basis is logged with the supplement name, the due date missed and the corrective filing date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Controller signs off on every not-applicable determination and on any supplement re-filed after its due date

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every supplement, exhibit and interrogatory listed in the reporting year's NAIC supplement index for the company's Blank type, for each writing company - both those filed and those declared not applicable

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every applicable supplement filed by its own due date with zero source-data differences; any supplement omitted without a written not-applicable basis citing the instruction is a fail regardless of materiality

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual across two due-date waves; test runs once a year in May covering both the March 1 and April 1 waves

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared or reviewed any sampled supplement and must sit outside the Controller organization

Evidence location for test results.value: Supplement completeness test workpaper (supplement index, applicability decisions, source tie-outs, timeliness recomputation, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under the reporting year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: A supplement register showing each supplement, its due date, its filed date, its barcode identifier and its source tie-out, producible for a financial examination information request within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Statutory Reporting Manager answers examiner questions on supplement content; the Chief Financial Officer clears any response conceding an omitted or misstated supplement, and the Appointed Actuary answers questions on the experience exhibits

checklist.step: Rebuild the supplement inventory from the reporting year's NAIC instructions
actions: Open the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions supplement index for the company's Blank type and list every supplement, exhibit and interrogatory named there.
For each entry capture the due date (March 1, March 15, April 1, June 1 or August 1) and whether it is filed with the state, the NAIC, or both.
Compare this year's list to last year's register and highlight every supplement added, retired or renamed by the Blanks (E) Working Group.
Publish the supplement inventory to the statutory close folder before January 15 so preparers have six weeks on the March 1 wave.
checklist.done: the inventory names every supplement in the current-year instructions with its due date and filing destination, and year-on-year changes are highlighted.

checklist.step: Decide applicability for each supplement and document the not-applicable calls
actions: Test each supplement against the company profile: lines of business written, Blank type, whether Medicare supplement, long-term care, credit or accident and health business exists, and whether the company holds trusteed assets.
Mark each supplement APPLICABLE or NOT APPLICABLE on the register.

For each NOT APPLICABLE call, quote the instruction sentence that scopes the supplement and state the company fact that puts it out of scope (for example, no Medicare supplement premium written in the reporting year).
Never leave a supplement marked simply 'N/A' - the quoted instruction and the company fact are both required.
Route all not-applicable calls to the Controller for sign-off.
checklist.done: every supplement carries an applicability decision, and each not-applicable call quotes the scoping instruction and the company fact behind it.

checklist.step: Assign a named preparer and reviewer to each applicable supplement
actions: Assign each applicable supplement a preparer and an independent reviewer by name, not by team.

Assign the source-data owner for each: HR for compensation data, Reinsurance Accounting for the attestation, Investment Operations for the investment interrogatories, Actuarial for the experience exhibits.
Set an internal due date one week ahead of each supplement's NAIC due date to leave room for review.
Circulate the assignment matrix and get each preparer to acknowledge their supplements in writing.
checklist.done: every applicable supplement has a named preparer, reviewer, source-data owner and an internal due date one week ahead of the NAIC date.

checklist.step: Prepare the Supplemental Compensation Exhibit
actions: Request from the Compensation and Benefits Manager the reporting-year compensation detail for the officers, directors and highest-paid employees the instruction scopes in.
Populate the exhibit with each individual's name, title and total compensation on the basis the instruction prescribes, including salary, bonus and other compensation components.
Reconcile the exhibit totals to the payroll expense recorded in the general ledger and explain any difference between accrual and paid basis.
Have the Chief HR Officer confirm the individual list is complete before it leaves Finance.
File the exhibit for submission with the March 1 wave and retain the payroll extract as source evidence.
checklist.done: the compensation exhibit lists every in-scope individual, reconciles to payroll expense, and is confirmed complete by the Chief HR Officer.

checklist.step: Prepare Schedule SIS and the stockholder information filings
actions: Pull the current stockholder record and the board-approved officer and director list from the corporate records.
Complete Schedule SIS - Stockholder Information Supplement with the ownership detail the instruction requires, filed with the domiciliary regulator by March 1.
Confirm the holding company structure shown agrees to Schedule Y Part 1 in the annual statement - a difference between them will be found on examination.
Have the General Counsel review the ownership disclosures before filing.
Retain the board resolution and stockholder register extract behind the schedule.
checklist.done: Schedule SIS is complete, agrees to Schedule Y, is counsel-reviewed and is ready for the March 1 wave.

checklist.step: Prepare the Reinsurance Attestation Supplement
actions: Assemble the reinsurance contracts in force at December 31 from the treaty repository and confirm each is signed by all parties within the period the instruction allows.

Answer each attestation representation: that no separate written or oral agreement reduces the reinsurer's obligations, that documentation is complete, and that risk transfer has been assessed for each contract.
Where any representation cannot be made cleanly, list the contract and the reason and escalate to the Chief Financial Officer before signature.
Obtain the chief executive officer and chief financial officer signatures the attestation requires.
File the signed attestation with the March 1 wave and retain the contract inventory behind it.
checklist.done: a fully signed reinsurance attestation is on file with a supporting contract inventory and every exception escalated before signature.

checklist.step: Prepare the Trusteed Surplus Statement where trusteed assets exist
actions: Obtain the trustee's December 31 statement of assets held in trust for the benefit of United States policyholders.
Populate the Trusteed Surplus Statement with trusteed assets, liabilities of the United States branch, and the resulting trusteed surplus.
Reconcile the trusteed asset detail to Schedule E Part 3 special deposits and to the trustee statement, security by security.
Where the company holds no trusteed assets, record the not-applicable basis rather than filing an empty statement.
File with the March 1 wave and retain the trustee statement as third-party evidence.
checklist.done: trusteed surplus reconciles to the trustee statement and to Schedule E Part 3, or a documented not-applicable basis is on file.

checklist.step: Prepare the health and long-term care experience exhibits
actions: Extract earned premium, incurred claims and policy counts for Medicare supplement business by state and by standardized plan for the Medicare Supplement Insurance Experience Exhibit, due March 1.
Extract accident and health experience by line for the Accident and Health Policy Experience Exhibit, due April 1.
Extract long-term care in-force counts, premium and claim experience for the Long-Term Care Experience Reporting Forms, due April 1.
Reconcile each exhibit's earned premium and incurred claims totals to the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit and to Schedule H where the Blank includes it.
Have the Appointed Actuary review the loss ratios reported before the exhibits are filed.
checklist.done: each experience exhibit reconciles to the annual statement premium and claim totals and carries an actuarial review.

checklist.step: Prepare the Supplemental Investment Risk Interrogatories
actions: Compute total admitted assets from Page 2 as the denominator every interrogatory percentage runs off.

Answer the concentration interrogatories: the ten largest exposures to a single issuer, the largest holdings by NAIC designation, the largest foreign exposures by country and currency, and the largest equity, real estate and mortgage exposures.
Compute each holding as a percentage of total admitted assets and check the ranking is genuinely by amount and not by portfolio label.
Answer the derivative, securities lending and repurchase interrogatories from Schedules DB and DL.
Cross-check every interrogatory answer back to Schedule D, DA, DB, DL and E and file the reconciliation before the April 1 deadline.
checklist.done: every investment interrogatory answer reconciles to the underlying schedule and to Page 2 total admitted assets, ready before April 1.

checklist.step: Draft Management's Discussion and Analysis
actions: Draft the MD&A covering results of operations, underwriting results by line, investment performance, liquidity and capital resources, and material year-on-year movements.
Quantify each explanation against the annual statement pages - a movement explained in words but not tied to a Page 4 line will be queried on examination.
Cover reserve development from Schedule P Part 2 and explain any adverse development in the year.
Route the draft to the Chief Financial Officer and the General Counsel for review, and to the Appointed Actuary for the reserve narrative.
File the approved MD&A with the domiciliary regulator by April 1.
checklist.done: the MD&A explains every material movement with a figure tied to a statement page and is CFO-approved before April 1.

checklist.step: Review each drafted supplement against its own instruction
actions: For each supplement, open the instruction page and walk the required columns and line items against the draft, field by field.
Check the reporting period, the company identifiers and the units of measure (whole dollars versus thousands) match what the instruction demands.
Confirm the independent reviewer named on the assignment matrix has signed the preparation workpaper.
Return any supplement with a blank required field to its preparer rather than filing it incomplete.
checklist.done: each supplement has been walked against its instruction field by field and carries a reviewer signature.

checklist.step: Run the cross-tie between supplements and the annual statement
actions: Build a tie-out sheet listing each supplement figure that must agree to an annual statement line, naming the page and line on both sides.
Tie experience exhibit premium to the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit, investment interrogatory percentages to Page 2 total admitted assets, and the compensation exhibit total to general expense.
Investigate and clear every difference before filing - a supplement that disagrees with the statement is the single most common examination finding.
File the tie-out sheet as the supporting workpaper for the supplement wave.
checklist.done: every supplement figure that must agree to a statement line does agree, and the tie-out sheet is filed.

checklist.step: File each supplement to its own destination and deadline
actions: Generate the NAIC barcode cover sheet for each supplement using the correct document type code and attach it as the first page.
Upload the March 1 wave supplements to the NAIC Financial Data Repository and to the domiciliary Division of Insurance channel on or before March 1.
Upload the April 1 wave supplements the same way on or before April 1, and file the confidential Actuarial Opinion Summary with the domiciliary regulator only, by March 15.
Capture each submission confirmation and write the filed date and barcode identifier onto the supplement register row.
Report the wave status to the Controller within 3 business days of each due date.
checklist.done: every applicable supplement shows a filed date on or before its own deadline with a captured confirmation and barcode identifier.

checklist.step: Close the supplement register and reconcile it to the inventory
actions: Count the inventory entries marked APPLICABLE and count the register rows carrying a filed date and confirmation.
Investigate each difference by supplement name - either it was filed and the confirmation was not captured, or it was not filed.
Confirm each not-applicable row still carries its quoted instruction and company fact, and the Controller sign-off.
Declare the supplement wave closed in writing to the Controller only when the counts agree.
checklist.done: applicable-supplement and filed-supplement counts agree and the wave closure is confirmed in writing to the Controller.

checklist.step: Archive the supplement evidence set
actions: Assemble each supplement's filed PDF, source extract, tie-out sheet, reviewer sign-off and submission confirmation into a reporting-year supplement evidence set.
Include the not-applicable justifications with their Controller sign-offs so the omissions are as evidenced as the filings.
Apply the 7-year retention label running from the March 1 statement date, extended through the next financial examination.
Confirm the set is searchable by supplement name, reporting year and NAIC company code.
checklist.done: the supplement evidence set covers both filings and documented omissions, is retention-labelled and is searchable by supplement name.

testing.step: Build the population of supplements owed for the reporting year
actions: Take the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions supplement index for the company's Blank type as the independent source, not the internal inventory.
List every supplement, exhibit and interrogatory with its due date and filing destination, by writing company.
Compare your list to the internal supplement inventory and list any entry the company omitted from its own inventory - an omission there guarantees an omission downstream.
Sign the population as complete and record the instruction edition used.
testing.done: the population is built from the NAIC instruction index itself and every internal-inventory omission is listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the supplement register to the population
actions: Match each population entry to a register row marked either filed or not applicable.
List every population entry with no register row as an automatic exception.
Confirm each not-applicable row quotes the scoping instruction and states the company fact, and carries a dated Controller sign-off.
Treat a bare 'N/A' with no quoted instruction as an unsupported omission, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every supplement in the population is matched to a filed row or a fully supported not-applicable row.

testing.step: Draw and document the supplement sample
actions: Take 100% of the Reinsurance Attestation Supplement, the Supplemental Investment Risk Interrogatories and Management's Discussion and Analysis.
Take 100% of every supplement marked not applicable, since the omission carries the greater risk.
Select 5 further supplements at random (seeded, reproducible) from the remainder.
Record the seed, the population count and the selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers the three highest-risk supplements and every not-applicable call, and is reproducible.

testing.step: Challenge every not-applicable determination
actions: For each not-applicable supplement, read the scoping instruction yourself and identify the fact that would bring the company into scope.
Test that fact independently - for a Medicare supplement omission, run a premium extract by product to confirm zero Medicare supplement premium was written or in force in the year.
For a trusteed surplus omission, confirm with Treasury that no assets are held in trust for United States policyholders.
Report any supplement omitted while the scoping fact is actually present as a failure to file, escalated the day it is found.
testing.done: each not-applicable call is independently tested against a data extract and any in-scope omission is escalated immediately.

testing.step: Re-perform the investment risk interrogatory computations
actions: Pull the December 31 holdings file independently and aggregate exposures by issuer to build your own ten-largest list.
Compare your ranking and amounts to the filed interrogatory answers, including the percentage of total admitted assets on each line.
Confirm the denominator used equals Page 2 total admitted assets as filed.
Recompute the foreign exposure and derivative answers from Schedules DB and DL and list every difference.
testing.done: the ten-largest exposures and their percentages are independently recomputed and every difference from the filed answers is listed.

testing.step: Tie the experience exhibits back to the annual statement and source systems
actions: Extract earned premium and incurred claims by line and by state directly from the policy administration and claims systems.
Compare to the Medicare Supplement Insurance Experience Exhibit, the Accident and Health Policy Experience Exhibit and the Long-Term Care Experience Reporting Forms as filed.
Confirm each exhibit's totals agree to the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit and to Schedule H where the Blank includes it.
Recompute the reported loss ratios and compare to the filed figures.
testing.done: each experience exhibit ties to independent system extracts and to the annual statement, and loss ratios recompute.

testing.step: Test the reinsurance attestation against the underlying contracts
actions: Select 15 reinsurance contracts in force at December 31 from the treaty repository.
Confirm each is signed by all parties and that the signature date falls within the period the attestation instruction permits.
Confirm a risk transfer assessment exists for each contract and reaches a documented conclusion.
Confirm the attestation carries the chief executive officer and chief financial officer signatures and that no contract escalated before signature was left unresolved.
testing.done: every sampled contract is fully executed within the permitted period with a risk transfer conclusion, and the attestation is properly signed.

testing.step: Recompute supplement timeliness and verify the barcode filings
actions: Open the NAIC Financial Data Repository filing history for the company and reporting year and read the filed date and document type for each supplement.
Compare each filed date to that supplement's own due date - March 1, March 15, April 1, June 1 or August 1 - and compute days late.
Confirm each supplement was filed under the correct document type code, since a right document under the wrong code does not register as filed.
Confirm the domiciliary-only supplements reached the Division of Insurance and not merely the NAIC.
testing.done: days-late is computed for every supplement against its own deadline and every document type code is verified in the repository.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the supplement, its due date, the days late or the unsupported omission, and the statement figure it disagreed with.
Assign a root cause (supplement dropped from the inventory, instruction change missed, source data late, tie-out skipped, wrong document type code) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any supplement never filed, file it immediately with a covering explanation cleared by the Controller.
Carry every open exception into the next reporting year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception names the supplement, its deadline miss or data difference, a root cause, an owner and a remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the completeness rate (applicable supplements filed on time divided by applicable supplements owed) and compare to the zero-omission threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references for each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared no sampled supplement and sits outside the Controller organization, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper under the reporting year and NAIC company code.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with the completeness rate, a stated conclusion and an Audit Committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual statutory audit engagement, the June 1 audited financial report filing and the August 1 internal control communications required under the NAIC Annual Financial Reporting Model Regulation

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the NAIC Annual Financial Reporting Model Regulation (Model 205) as enacted in Alaska and administered by the Alaska Division of Insurance, covering the June 1 audited statutory financial report, CPA independence and partner rotation, the audit committee requirements and the five-business-day adverse financial condition notification

In-scope processes.value: Auditor appointment and independence confirmation, audit committee oversight, delivery of the statutory audit workpaper request list, the audit of the SAP-basis financial statements underlying the March 1 annual statement, and filing of the audited report, the internal control communication and Management's Report of Internal Control over Financial Reporting

In-scope systems.value: Audit request list, control documentation and management representation tracking, with the ERP general ledger as the audit source and the filed audited report stored in the financial reporting repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statutory Audit Coordination Procedure — auditor appointment and notification, independence and rotation checks, PBC list management, audit adjustment protocol, management representation letter, and the June 1 and August 1 filing steps

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Audit Committee and reviewed annually at the Committee's first meeting of the calendar year alongside the auditor reappointment

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Auditor appointment notice to the domiciliary regulator within 60 days of retaining the accountant; audited statutory financial report by June 1; Communication of Internal Control Related Matters Noted in an Audit by August 1; Management's Report of Internal Control over Financial Reporting by August 1 where direct plus assumed premium exceeds the $500 million threshold; adverse financial condition notification within 5 business days of the auditor's determination

Deadline reminders configured.value: Audit calendar alerts at March 15 (fieldwork start), April 30 (draft report), May 15 (management representation letter due), May 25 (June 1 filing package ready) and July 15 (August 1 internal control package ready), addressed to the Controller and copied to the Audit Committee chair

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Engagement letter, independence and partner rotation confirmations, the signed audit opinion, the audit adjustment schedule, the management representation letter, the internal control communication and the filing confirmations, retained 7 years from the June 1 filing date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any audit adjustment that changes filed statutory surplus, any modified or qualified opinion, any independence breach and any late June 1 or August 1 filing is logged with the dollar effect and the regulator notification made

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Chief Audit Executive, reporting to the Audit Committee, signs off on remediation of every material weakness and significant deficiency raised in the auditor's internal control communication

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The reporting year's audit engagement per writing company: the engagement and independence documentation, the audit adjustment schedule, the filed audited statutory financial report, the internal control communication and the management internal control report where the premium threshold is met

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Audited report filed by June 1 and internal control communications by August 1 with no exception; any unadjusted audit difference affecting statutory surplus that was not reflected in an amended annual statement is a fail; any independence or partner rotation breach is a fail regardless of effect

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; test runs once a year in September after the August 1 internal control filings have closed the cycle
