Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have coordinated the audit, prepared any audited schedule or sat in the Controller organization

Evidence location for test results.value: Statutory audit compliance test workpaper (engagement documentation review, independence checks, adjustment reconciliation, filing timeliness, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under the reporting year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Engagement letter, independence and rotation confirmations, signed audit opinion, audit adjustment schedule and both filing confirmations, assembled as a Division of Insurance Model 205 compliance response within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Controller answers Division of Insurance questions on the audited report; the Audit Committee chair owns any communication about auditor independence or a modified opinion, and the Chief Financial Officer makes the five-business-day adverse financial condition notification personally

checklist.step: Confirm the independent accountant's appointment and notify the regulator
actions: Record the Audit Committee's resolution appointing or reappointing the independent certified public accountant for the reporting year.
Send the domiciliary Division of Insurance written notice of the accountant retained within 60 days of the engagement, naming the firm and the engagement partner.

Obtain the accountant's letter stating awareness of the Model 205 requirements and that the accountant will notify the regulator within five business days of any determination that the insurer does not meet minimum capital and surplus.
File the resolution, the notice and the awareness letter in the corporate record and copy them to the Controller.
checklist.done: the appointment is board-recorded, the regulator notice is sent within 60 days, and the accountant's awareness letter is on file.

checklist.step: Test the accountant's independence and partner rotation
actions: Obtain the firm's written independence confirmation for the reporting year addressed to the Audit Committee.
Check the lead and concurring audit partners against the rotation limit - no more than five consecutive years, with the required time off before return.

List every non-audit service the firm performed for the company in the year and test each against the prohibited services list, including bookkeeping, actuarial services affecting the audited amounts, internal audit outsourcing and management functions.
Confirm the Audit Committee pre-approved each permitted non-audit service and the fee, and that the fees are disclosed to the Committee.
Escalate any partner over the rotation limit or any prohibited service to the Audit Committee chair before fieldwork begins.
checklist.done: independence is confirmed in writing, partner rotation is within the limit, and every non-audit service is pre-approved and permitted.

checklist.step: Confirm the Audit Committee meets the Model 205 composition requirement
actions: List the Audit Committee members and test each against the independence definition in the regulation.
Compute the company's prior-year direct plus assumed premium to determine which independence proportion applies to the Committee.
Confirm the Committee's charter gives it responsibility for appointing, compensating and overseeing the accountant, and for the accountant's direct reporting line.
Where the company relies on a parent's audit committee, document the reliance and confirm the parent committee meets the same requirement.
File the composition assessment with the Committee minutes.
checklist.done: Audit Committee composition is tested against the premium-scaled independence requirement and the assessment is minuted.

checklist.step: Agree the audit timetable and issue the prepared-by-client list
actions: Hold the planning meeting with the engagement partner and agree fieldwork start, draft report date, clearance meeting and the June 1 filing date working backwards from it.
Load the auditor's prepared-by-client request list into the audit management platform with an owner and a due date on every item.

Map each request to its source: trial balance and adjustment register from the ERP, Schedule D holdings from investment accounting, Schedule P triangles from reserving, Schedule F detail from ceded accounting.
Set weekly status reporting on open requests to the Controller and flag any item at risk of delaying the June 1 date.
Confirm the engagement letter is signed before fieldwork opens.
checklist.done: a signed engagement letter and a fully owned request list exist, with the timetable working backwards from June 1.

checklist.step: Deliver the statutory-basis financial statements to the auditor
actions: Prepare the statutory-basis balance sheet, statement of operations, changes in capital and surplus and cash flow for the reporting year, together with the statutory notes.
Confirm each statement agrees to the corresponding page of the filed March 1 annual statement - Page 2, Page 3, Page 4 and Page 5 - line by line.
Disclose every permitted or prescribed practice used and quantify its effect on surplus in the notes.
Hand the statements to the auditor with the crosswalk to the filed annual statement attached.
Any difference between the audited statements and the filed statement must be explained now, not at the clearance meeting.
checklist.done: the statutory-basis statements agree to the filed annual statement pages and every permitted practice is quantified in the notes.

checklist.step: Support the auditor's substantive testing on the high-risk balances
actions: Provide the loss and LAE reserve support: the Reserving Actuary's report, the Schedule P triangles and the reconciliation of booked reserves to the actuarial indication.
Provide investment support: the custodian confirmation, the Schedule D holdings file with NAIC designations and the amortization schedules.
Provide reinsurance support: the Schedule F recoverable detail by reinsurer, the collateral documents and the treaty inventory.
Provide premium support: the unearned premium register reconciled to the GL and the agents' balances aging behind the non-admitted amount.
Answer each auditor query in the audit platform within 3 business days and keep the response with the request so the trail survives.
checklist.done: each high-risk balance has third-party or system-generated support delivered and every auditor query is answered within 3 business days.

checklist.step: Work the audit adjustment schedule and decide what must be corrected
actions: Take the auditor's schedule of proposed audit adjustments and unadjusted differences and assess each for its effect on statutory surplus.
Book every adjustment the company accepts to the statutory ledger with the SSAP reference and the audit reference on the journal.
For each difference left unadjusted, document the reason and its surplus effect, and confirm the aggregate remains below the threshold agreed with the auditor and the Audit Committee.
Where an accepted adjustment changes the surplus already reported on March 1, open the amended annual statement assessment with the Statutory Reporting Manager the same week.
Present the full schedule to the Audit Committee before the opinion is signed.
checklist.done: every proposed adjustment is booked or documented as unadjusted with a surplus effect, and any March 1 surplus change triggers an amendment assessment.

checklist.step: Sign the management representation letter
actions: Read the representation letter line by line and test each representation against evidence rather than recollection.
Confirm the representations on completeness of records, related party transactions, reinsurance with no side agreements, litigation and claims, subsequent events and permitted practices.
Obtain the General Counsel's legal letter response covering litigation and claims before signing.
Sign the letter dated the same date as the audit report and file it with the audit evidence.
Refuse to sign any representation that cannot be supported - a qualified representation is better than an unsupported one.
checklist.done: a signed management representation letter dated with the audit report exists, backed by the legal letter response.

checklist.step: Receive the audit opinion and take the Audit Committee through it
actions: Obtain the signed audit report on the statutory-basis financial statements and confirm the opinion type - unmodified, qualified, adverse or disclaimer.
Hold the Audit Committee clearance meeting with the engagement partner present and the Controller excused for the private session.
Take the Committee through the adjustment schedule, the unadjusted differences and any control matters raised.
Where the opinion is other than unmodified, notify the domiciliary Division of Insurance and escalate to the board the same week.
Minute the Committee's acceptance of the audited financial statements.
checklist.done: a signed opinion is accepted by the Audit Committee in minuted session, with any modified opinion reported to the regulator that week.

checklist.step: File the audited statutory financial report by June 1
actions: Assemble the filing package: the audited statutory financial statements, the accountant's report, the notes and the report on any permitted practices.
Generate the NAIC barcode cover sheet under the audited financial statements document type and upload to the NAIC Financial Data Repository.
File with the domiciliary Division of Insurance and with every other jurisdiction whose state filing checklist row demands the audited report, on or before June 1.
Where an extension is needed, apply to the domiciliary commissioner in writing before June 1 showing the financial hardship basis, and file within the permission granted.
Capture every confirmation onto the filing register and report the status to the Controller within 3 business days.
checklist.done: the audited report is filed by June 1 with the NAIC and every required jurisdiction, with confirmations captured, or a pre-deadline extension is on record.

checklist.step: Obtain and file the Communication of Internal Control Related Matters
actions: Request from the accountant the written communication of unremediated material weaknesses in internal control over statutory financial reporting noted during the audit.
Where no material weakness was noted, obtain the accountant's written statement to that effect - the communication is filed either way.
Add management's description of the actions taken or planned for each matter noted, with an owner and a completion date.
File the communication with the domiciliary Division of Insurance by August 1 and capture the confirmation.
Load each matter into the audit management platform as a tracked remediation item.
checklist.done: the internal control communication, with management's remediation response, is filed by August 1 and every matter is tracked.

checklist.step: Prepare Management's Report of Internal Control over Financial Reporting where the threshold is met
actions: Compute prior-year direct written plus assumed premium and compare to the $500 million threshold that triggers the management report.
Where the threshold is met, document the control framework used, scope the controls over statutory financial reporting, and test them through the year.
State management's conclusion on effectiveness as of December 31 and disclose any unremediated material weakness.
Have the Chief Financial Officer and Chief Executive Officer sign the report.
File it with the domiciliary Division of Insurance by August 1, or document the exemption computation where the threshold is not met.
checklist.done: the management internal control report is signed and filed by August 1, or the below-threshold exemption computation is documented.

checklist.step: Run the five-business-day adverse condition notification protocol
actions: Brief the engagement partner at planning that any determination that the insurer does not meet minimum capital and surplus, or that a material misstatement exists, triggers a five-business-day notification to the domiciliary regulator.
On receiving any such determination, notify the Alaska Division of Insurance in writing within five business days, stating the finding and the company's response.
Notify the Audit Committee chair and the board the same day, and engage the General Counsel on the wording of the regulator notice.
Log the determination, the notification date and the regulator's response in the issue tracker.
Never wait for the audit report to be issued before making the notification - the clock runs from the determination.
checklist.done: any adverse determination is notified to the domiciliary regulator within five business days, with board notification the same day and the exchange logged.

checklist.step: Track remediation of every control matter through to closure
actions: Open a remediation item for each material weakness and significant deficiency with an owner, a control description and a target date.
Test the remediated control operating over a period sufficient to conclude on effectiveness before closing the item.
Report open items to the Audit Committee at each meeting with days open and the target date.
Carry any item still open at the next year-end into the next audit's communication as a recurring matter.
Obtain the Chief Audit Executive's sign-off before an item is closed.
checklist.done: every control matter has an owner, a tested remediation and a Chief Audit Executive sign-off before closure.

checklist.step: Archive the audit evidence set for the reporting year
actions: Assemble the engagement letter, regulator appointment notice, independence and rotation confirmations, audited statements, signed opinion, adjustment schedule, representation letter, internal control communication and all filing confirmations.
Apply the 7-year retention label running from the June 1 filing date, extended through the next financial examination.
Confirm the set is searchable by reporting year, NAIC company code and document type.
Hand the index reference to the Audit Committee chair and the Compliance Officer.
checklist.done: the reporting-year audit evidence set is complete, retention-labelled and retrievable by year, company code and document type.

testing.step: Build the population of Model 205 obligations for the reporting year
actions: List, for each writing company, every Model 205 deliverable: the appointment notice, the awareness letter, the audited statutory financial report, the internal control communication and the management internal control report where the premium threshold is met.
Confirm the threshold determination by pulling prior-year direct plus assumed written premium from the annual statement rather than accepting the internal computation.
Add every jurisdiction whose state filing checklist row demands the audited report, so the population covers distribution as well as production.
Sign the population as complete and record the extraction date.
testing.done: the population lists every Model 205 deliverable and every jurisdiction owed the audited report, with the premium threshold independently computed.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to filed and retained evidence
actions: Match each population entry to a filed document with a dated confirmation in the repository.
List every entry with no evidence as an automatic exception, including a missing awareness letter or appointment notice.
Confirm the audited report reached every jurisdiction in the population, not only the domiciliary state.
State the unmatched count before any sampling begins.
testing.done: every Model 205 deliverable is matched to dated evidence or listed as an exception with the count stated.

testing.step: Re-perform the independence and partner rotation checks
actions: Read the firm's independence confirmation letter and check it is addressed to the Audit Committee and dated within the reporting year.
Independently count the consecutive years the lead and concurring partners have served on the engagement from prior-year audit reports.
Pull the accounts payable ledger for all payments to the audit firm in the year and reconcile the services behind them to the Audit Committee's pre-approval record.
Test any service not on the pre-approval record against the prohibited services list and report a breach immediately, not at report date.
testing.done: partner tenure is independently counted, every payment to the firm reconciles to a pre-approved permitted service, and any breach is reported immediately.

testing.step: Verify the Audit Committee composition and oversight record
actions: Test each Audit Committee member against the regulation's independence definition using the director questionnaires and related party disclosures.
Confirm the proportion of independent members meets the level required at the company's premium volume.
Read the Committee minutes for the clearance meeting and confirm the private session with the accountant took place without management present.
Confirm the Committee minuted its acceptance of the audited financial statements before the June 1 filing.
testing.done: Committee composition meets the premium-scaled requirement and the minutes evidence a private session and a pre-filing acceptance.

testing.step: Reconcile the audited statements to the filed annual statement
actions: Compare the audited statutory balance sheet and statement of operations line by line to Pages 2, 3 and 4 of the annual statement as filed on March 1.
Quantify every difference and trace it to an audit adjustment on the auditor's schedule.
Where a difference changes reported statutory surplus, confirm an amended annual statement was filed with the NAIC and all jurisdictions that received the original.
Treat a surplus-changing difference with no amended filing as a reportable regulatory exception, not a presentation matter.
testing.done: every difference between the audited statements and the filed statement traces to an adjustment, and surplus-changing differences show an amended filing.

testing.step: Test the audit adjustment and unadjusted difference schedules
actions: Take the auditor's adjustment schedule and trace every accepted adjustment to a posted journal in the statutory ledger with the SSAP and audit references on it.
Sum the unadjusted differences, including the prior-year rollover effect, and compare to the materiality threshold agreed with the Audit Committee.
Confirm each unadjusted difference carries a written reason and a surplus effect.
Confirm the schedule presented to the Audit Committee matches the auditor's final schedule.
testing.done: every accepted adjustment is traced to a posted journal, and unadjusted differences are summed and evidenced against the agreed threshold.

testing.step: Recompute the June 1 and August 1 filing timeliness
actions: Open the NAIC Financial Data Repository filing history and read the filed dates for the audited financial statements and the internal control documents.
Compute days late against June 1 for the audited report and against August 1 for the internal control communication and the management internal control report.
Where an extension was used, confirm the written request pre-dated June 1 and the domiciliary commissioner's permission is on file, and measure against the extended date.
Confirm the appointment notice was sent within 60 days of the engagement by comparing the engagement letter date to the notice date.
testing.done: days-late is computed against June 1, August 1 and the 60-day notice rule, with any extension permission verified on file.

testing.step: Test control matter remediation and the adverse condition protocol
actions: Pull every material weakness and significant deficiency raised in the current and prior year communications and check each has an owner, a target date and a tested remediation.
Re-perform the remediation test on 5 closed items and confirm the control actually operated over the stated period.
Check whether any adverse financial condition determination arose in the year and, if so, recompute the five-business-day notification window from the determination date to the regulator notice date.
Flag any item closed on assertion alone, without an operating-effectiveness test, as an exception.
testing.done: every control matter has a tested remediation, 5 closures are re-performed, and any adverse determination notification is recomputed against the five-business-day window.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the Model 205 deliverable, the deadline missed or the requirement breached, and the surplus or regulatory effect.
Assign a root cause (late audit fieldwork, unresolved request list item, missed threshold computation, independence lapse, notification protocol not triggered) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date ahead of the next audit planning meeting and, for any independence breach, escalate to the Audit Committee chair the day it is logged.
Carry every open exception into the next reporting year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception names the deliverable, the breach, a root cause, an owner and a remediation date, with independence breaches escalated same-day.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Summarise the results against the thresholds: on-time June 1 and August 1 filings, zero independence breaches, and no unamended surplus-changing difference.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither coordinated the audit nor sits in the Controller organization, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper under the reporting year and NAIC company code.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with a stated conclusion, the filing timeliness results and an Audit Committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the rolling 51-jurisdiction statutory filing calendar, its annual refresh against the NAIC state filing checklist, and the evidence-of-timeliness file that proves each deadline was met

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — each jurisdiction's financial reporting statute and filing bulletins, reconciled to the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions state filing checklist appendix; the Alaska Division of Insurance row is the domiciliary anchor and drives the March 1 annual and 15th-of-month quarterly dates

In-scope processes.value: Continuous calendar maintenance: annual rebuild of the jurisdiction matrix, monitoring of state bulletins for changed due dates, media and fees, licensing-change intake that adds or removes a jurisdiction, reminder configuration, and the running proof-of-timeliness register across all statutory filing types

In-scope systems.value: The jurisdiction filing calendar and filing register, with confirmations stored in the compliance evidence repository and open items driven through the regulatory filing tracker

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statutory Filing Calendar Maintenance Procedure — annual rebuild from the NAIC state filing checklist, bulletin monitoring cadence, licensing-change trigger, reminder configuration standard and the monthly calendar-to-register reconciliation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Controller and re-approved each January after the calendar rebuild, with interim changes approved by the Regulatory Reporting Manager and logged

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Every statutory deadline in the calendar: annual statement and RBC March 1, Actuarial Opinion Summary March 15, April 1 supplements, audited financials June 1, internal control communications August 1, and quarterly statements May 15, August 15 and November 15, each held per jurisdiction with that state's own variation

Deadline reminders configured.value: Every calendar row carries automatic reminders at T-30, T-14, T-7, T-3 and T-1 business days to the named preparer, with T-3 escalation to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and T-1 escalation to the Controller for any row still open

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Dated captures of each jurisdiction's requirement source (state filing checklist page or bulletin), the calendar version history showing what changed and when, and every filing confirmation, retained 7 years from the filing date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any calendar row missing a verification date inside the current year, any deadline changed by a state that the calendar did not pick up, and any filing with no confirmation is logged with the jurisdiction, the discovery date and the correction

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Controller signs off on the annual calendar rebuild, on every mid-year change to a jurisdiction's due date or medium, and on the disposition of any missed deadline

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every row of the jurisdiction filing calendar for the year - 51 jurisdictions times each statutory filing type times each writing company - together with the licensing register that determines which rows should exist

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every calendar row carries a due date, a medium, a named owner, configured reminders and a verification date inside the current filing year; any jurisdiction where the company holds a certificate of authority but the calendar carries no row is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; the calendar completeness test runs quarterly after each filing cycle closes, with the full rebuild verification performed in the first quarter after the January refresh

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not maintain the calendar or transmit filings, and must sit outside the Regulatory Reporting team

Evidence location for test results.value: Filing calendar completeness test workpaper (licensing reconciliation, row-attribute testing, bulletin sweep re-performance, reminder evidence, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository, indexed by quarter

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The jurisdiction calendar with source references and verification dates, plus the timeliness register showing each filing's due date and confirmation date, producible for a Division of Insurance timeliness inquiry within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Reporting Manager answers state filing-desk timeliness queries from the register; the Controller clears any response conceding a missed deadline, and General Counsel is engaged where a penalty or administrative proceeding follows

checklist.step: Rebuild the jurisdiction filing calendar every January
actions: Open the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions state filing checklist appendix and rebuild the calendar jurisdiction by jurisdiction rather than rolling last year's forward.
For each of the 51 jurisdictions create one row per filing type: annual statement, RBC report, quarterly statements, each supplement, audited financials and internal control communications.
Populate each row with the due date, the medium, the copy count, the notarization requirement, the fee and the filing channel.
Diff the rebuilt calendar against last year's version and list every changed cell for the Controller's approval.
Version the calendar as CAL-<yyyy>-v1 and lock the prior year's version read-only.
checklist.done: a versioned current-year calendar exists with one row per jurisdiction per filing type and a Controller-approved change list against the prior year.

checklist.step: Attach a dated source capture to every calendar row
actions: For each jurisdiction print the state filing checklist page or the state's own filing instructions page to PDF, named <state>-filing-requirements-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf.
Link the capture to every calendar row it supports so the row's due date and medium can be defended without re-researching.
Write the verification date onto the row - a row whose verification date is older than the current filing year is treated as unverified.
Flag any jurisdiction whose published instructions could not be located and escalate it to the Regulatory Reporting Manager rather than guessing the requirement.
checklist.done: every calendar row links to a dated source capture and carries a verification date inside the current filing year.

checklist.step: Reconcile the calendar to the certificate of authority register
actions: Pull the licensing register listing every jurisdiction in which each writing company holds a certificate of authority, with the licence status and line authority.
Match each licensed jurisdiction to calendar rows for that company and list any licensed jurisdiction with no rows.
List any calendar row for a jurisdiction where the licence has been surrendered or suspended and confirm with Compliance whether a final filing is still owed.
Correct the calendar the same week and record the licensing register version used for the reconciliation.
checklist.done: every licensed jurisdiction has calendar rows and every calendar row maps to a live licence or a documented run-off filing obligation.

checklist.step: Assign a named owner and preparer to every calendar row
actions: Assign each row an accountable owner by name - Statutory Reporting for statement production rows, Regulatory Reporting for transmission rows, Actuarial for the opinion rows, Controller for the audit rows.
Set an internal target date on each row at least 5 business days ahead of the regulatory due date.
Circulate the ownership list and require each owner to acknowledge their rows in writing before the first cycle of the year.
Reassign rows within one business day of any leaver or role change so no row is left ownerless.
checklist.done: every calendar row has a named owner who has acknowledged it and an internal target date ahead of the regulatory deadline.

checklist.step: Configure the reminder cascade on every row
actions: Set automated reminders on each row at T-30, T-14, T-7, T-3 and T-1 business days before the regulatory due date.
Route T-30 through T-7 to the named preparer, T-3 to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and T-1 to the Controller.
Send a test reminder on each newly created row and confirm it reaches the addressee's inbox - an unrouted reminder is the same as no reminder.
Record the reminder configuration and the test result on the row.
checklist.done: every row has a tested five-stage reminder cascade with escalation to the Manager at T-3 and the Controller at T-1.

checklist.step: Sweep state bulletins monthly for changed requirements
actions: On the first business day of each month open each state insurance department's bulletin and industry notice page and read entries published since the last sweep.
Look specifically for changes to statutory filing due dates, submission medium, electronic-filing mandates, fee schedules and notarization requirements.
Log each relevant bulletin with its number, issue date, the affected calendar rows and the change required.
Update the affected rows within 5 business days, re-version the calendar and notify the affected owners.
Record 'no change' explicitly for the month so the sweep itself is evidenced.
checklist.done: a dated monthly bulletin sweep log exists for every month with either logged changes applied within 5 business days or an explicit no-change record.

checklist.step: Trigger calendar changes off licensing and corporate events
actions: Subscribe the calendar owner to the licensing workflow so every new certificate of authority, licence surrender, redomestication and merger raises a calendar change task.
On a new licence, add the full row set for that jurisdiction and set the first due date, checking whether a partial-year statement is owed.
On a surrender or withdrawal, confirm the final statutory filing obligations before removing rows, since run-off filings usually continue.
On a redomestication, rebuild the domiciliary row set against the new home state's requirements.
Record the triggering event and its date on every row added or removed.
checklist.done: every licensing or corporate event produces a dated calendar change task, and no row is removed without confirming run-off obligations.

checklist.step: Run the weekly open-filing status review
actions: Each Monday produce the open-rows report showing every row with a due date inside the next 45 days and its current status.
Walk the report with the named owners and record a status per row: not started, in preparation, ready to file, filed pending confirmation, closed.
Escalate any row still 'not started' at T-14 to the Controller with the reason.
Publish the report to the statutory reporting distribution so no owner can claim they did not know a deadline was live.
checklist.done: a dated weekly open-rows report exists with a status against every row due inside 45 days and T-14 escalations recorded.

checklist.step: Record the filing and its confirmation onto the calendar row
actions: On each submission write the actual submission date, the channel used and the confirmation identifier onto the calendar row.
Link the stored confirmation artifact from the compliance evidence repository to the row.
Compute days early or late against the row's due date automatically and leave the computed value visible on the row.
Leave the row at 'filed pending confirmation' until the artifact is attached - never close a row on the strength of a submission alone.
checklist.done: every filed row shows a submission date, a confirmation identifier, a linked artifact and a computed days-early or days-late value.

checklist.step: Reconcile the calendar to the filing register monthly
actions: At each month end count the calendar rows with a due date in the month and the register rows carrying a confirmation for that month.
Investigate each difference by jurisdiction and filing type and record the resolution on the row.
Confirm no row closed in the month without a linked confirmation artifact.
Sign the monthly reconciliation and send it to the Controller within 5 business days of month end.
checklist.done: a signed monthly reconciliation exists showing calendar and register agreement, delivered to the Controller within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Report calendar health metrics to the Controller each quarter
actions: Build the quarterly metric set: on-time filing rate by jurisdiction, rows with a verification date older than the current year, rows with no owner, rows with no confirmation artifact, and bulletin changes applied within 5 business days.
Show the trend against the prior three quarters so deterioration is visible rather than inferred.
Present the metrics to the Controller and the Chief Financial Officer with a named action for every red measure.
File the pack in the compliance evidence repository as the quarterly control evidence.
checklist.done: a quarterly metric pack with trends and named actions is presented to the Controller and filed as control evidence.

checklist.step: Manage penalties, extension requests and regulator correspondence
actions: Log every late-filing notice, penalty assessment or filing deficiency letter received from any jurisdiction against the relevant calendar row.
Draft the response with the timeliness register evidence attached and have the Controller clear any admission of lateness before it is sent.
Where an extension is sought, submit the written request to the state before the due date and record the request, the approver and the extended date on the row.
Pay assessed penalties through Treasury and record the payment reference on the row so the matter closes on evidence.
checklist.done: every penalty or deficiency notice has a logged response, a cleared admission where relevant, and a recorded resolution on the calendar row.

checklist.step: Run the annual look-back over the closed filing year
actions: After the November 15 quarterly closes, run the full-year timeliness report across all jurisdictions and filing types.
Identify every row filed inside 3 business days of its deadline and treat the pattern as a process risk even where nothing was late.
Identify every requirement the calendar picked up late from a bulletin and shorten the sweep cadence for that state.
Feed the findings into the January rebuild so next year's calendar starts from the lessons of this one.
checklist.done: a full-year look-back report exists identifying near-misses and late-detected changes, feeding the January rebuild.

checklist.step: Prove the calendar to an examiner on demand
actions: Maintain a standing examination export: the current calendar with source captures, the timeliness register with confirmation identifiers, and the monthly reconciliations.
Test the export twice a year by producing it end to end within 5 business days as if an examiner had asked.
Confirm the export shows, for any jurisdiction an examiner names, the due date, the source of that due date, the filing date and the proof of receipt.
Record the rehearsal date, the elapsed time and any gap found.
checklist.done: a rehearsed examination export exists that answers due date, source, filing date and receipt for any named jurisdiction within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Archive the calendar version history and evidence set
actions: At year end archive the calendar version history, every source capture, the monthly bulletin sweep logs, the monthly reconciliations and the timeliness register.
Apply the 7-year retention label running from each filing date, extended through the next financial examination.
Confirm the archive is searchable by jurisdiction, filing type, reporting year and NAIC company code.
Hand the index reference to the Controller and the Chief Audit Executive.
checklist.done: the year's calendar and timeliness evidence is archived, retention-labelled and searchable by jurisdiction and filing type.

testing.step: Build the population of calendar rows that should exist
actions: Pull the certificate of authority register for every writing company and list each licensed jurisdiction with its licence status.
Multiply by the statutory filing types required for the company's Blank type from the current-year NAIC state filing checklist to build the expected row set.
Add rows for jurisdictions in run-off where filing obligations continue after licence surrender.
Sign the population as complete and record both the licensing register version and the instruction edition used.
testing.done: the expected row set is built from the licensing register and the NAIC checklist independently of the company's own calendar.

testing.step: Reconcile the maintained calendar to the expected row set
actions: Match every expected row to a calendar row on jurisdiction, company and filing type.
List every expected row with no calendar row - each is a jurisdiction the company cannot have been reminded to file in.
List every calendar row with no expected row and confirm it is a run-off obligation rather than a stale entry.
State the unmatched counts in both directions before sampling.
testing.done: unmatched rows are listed in both directions with counts stated, and every missing jurisdiction is named.

testing.step: Draw and document the calendar row sample
actions: Take 100% of the domiciliary jurisdiction rows and 100% of rows added or changed during the year.
Select 30 further rows at random (seeded, reproducible) spread across jurisdictions and filing types.
Include 100% of rows tied to a prior-year late filing or a penalty notice.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers the domiciliary and all changed rows, and includes every prior-year problem row.

testing.step: Re-perform the due date and medium research for sampled rows
actions: For each sampled row open the state's own filing instructions or the NAIC state filing checklist and reach your own conclusion on the due date, medium, copy count and fee before looking at the calendar row.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded row; any difference is an exception, including a right date supported by the wrong source.
Confirm the row's linked source capture is dated inside the current filing year and actually shows the requirement claimed.
Screenshot the source you relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled row has an independent re-performance of its due date and medium with a captured source page.

testing.step: Test row attributes for completeness
actions: For every calendar row in the population, test that a due date, medium, fee, named owner, internal target date and verification date are all present.
Count rows whose verification date pre-dates the current filing year and report the count as an aging measure, not a pass.
Confirm each named owner is a current employee by matching against the HR active roster.
Report the attribute completeness rate for the whole calendar rather than the sample only.
testing.done: attribute completeness is measured across the whole calendar and every ownerless, unverified or stale row is counted.

testing.step: Test that the reminder cascade actually fired
actions: For each sampled row with a deadline in the period, pull the system notification log and confirm reminders fired at T-30, T-14, T-7, T-3 and T-1.
Confirm the T-3 notification reached the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the T-1 notification reached the Controller where the row was still open.
Match the notification recipient to a live mailbox - a reminder addressed to a departed employee counts as not sent.
Report every row where any stage of the cascade did not fire.
testing.done: notification logs prove each stage of the cascade fired to a live recipient, and every missing stage is reported.

testing.step: Re-perform the bulletin sweep for a sampled quarter
actions: Pick one quarter and read the bulletin and industry notice pages of 10 state insurance departments for that period yourself.
Identify any bulletin changing a statutory filing due date, medium, electronic-filing mandate or fee.
Compare your findings to the monthly sweep logs and list anything the sweep missed.
For anything the sweep caught, recompute the elapsed days from bulletin issue date to calendar update and compare to the 5-business-day standard.
testing.done: an independent bulletin sweep of 10 states is performed for a quarter, with misses listed and application timeliness recomputed.

testing.step: Recompute timeliness across the closed cycles and test the examination export
actions: For every filing closed in the year, recompute days early or late as confirmation date minus due date using the state's own receipt-versus-postmark rule.
Compare your computed values to those held on the calendar rows and list any row whose computed value is understated.
Ask the Regulatory Reporting Manager to produce the examination export for 5 jurisdictions you name, and time the production.
Confirm the export shows the due date, its source, the filing date and the proof of receipt for each named jurisdiction.
testing.done: timeliness is independently recomputed for every closed filing and the examination export answers 5 named jurisdictions within 5 business days.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the jurisdiction, the filing type, the missing attribute or missed deadline and the regulatory consequence.

Assign a root cause (calendar rebuilt from last year rather than the instructions, licensing change not fed through, bulletin sweep missed, reminder routed to a departed employee, confirmation never attached) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date ahead of the next filing cycle and, for any missing jurisdiction row, add the row and file any overdue statement immediately.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception names the jurisdiction, the defect, a root cause, an owner and a remediation date, with missing rows added immediately.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the calendar completeness rate, the attribute completeness rate and the on-time filing rate, and compare each to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither maintains the calendar nor transmits filings, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper indexed by quarter and NAIC company code.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with the three completeness and timeliness rates, a stated conclusion and an Audit Committee reporting date.
